advisor_identified: J. L. (Jack Lawrence) Granatstein, historian of Canadian political and military history, York University History Department, 1966–1995.

evidence.says: York University archives identifies J. L. as Jack Lawrence Granatstein, lists Duke University (PhD, 1966), and places him in York’s History Department from 1966 to 1995.
The award biography lists Duke University (PhD, 1966) and York University History Department service from 1966 to 1995.

Megan Hamilton, “The Intellectual Career of J. L. Granatstein,” Waterloo Historical Review 10 (2021), pp. 20–21, states that he completed his Duke PhD in 1966, joined York’s History Department, and published his Duke doctoral thesis as The Politics of Survival: The Conservative Party of Canada, 1939-1945 in 1967.
Lists the 1966 thesis as The Conservative Party of Canada, 1939–1945 and the doctorate as a Duke University PhD.

notes: The linked record matches the advisor’s name, Duke institution, 1966 doctorate year and thesis subject/title; 1939-45 abbreviates 1939–1945. The exact thesis title is supported by Wikipedia and the supplied AHA record; no original thesis catalogue record was retrieved. The Waterloo article independently connects his Duke thesis to the 1967 book.
